allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 9 m tall and 25 cm across at breast height at 80 years in a closed stand. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: dark yellowish-green needles; thin, scaly, reddish-purple bark. Needle shoots (plant roadmap P4): flat needles 1 to 3 cm long and about 2 mm wide, so a needle 0.09 as wide as it is long (`width`), from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): thin purplish scales peeling to show red inner bark; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle`, `ranks` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated needles.

appearance.organs.spray.shape.needle.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

appearance.organs.spray.shape.ranks.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

appearance.spreads.organs.spray.shape.ne.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, slow, often crooked understory tree with long, drooping branches and flat sprays of soft, pointed needles. Not fitted to measurements. Cones (plant forms F3): seeds in a red fleshy aril about 8 mm; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Spec rework E6d: `needle_years` now set by the rules at Pinidae from the stated characters. Conifer form (pinidae revision 5): `branch_reach` fitted so the open-grown crown keeps revision 4's radius at the oldest keyframe, and `pipe_rings` refitted to the dbh references now that the crown holds more foliage; `branch_ageing` is gone with the calendar ageing it set.

generator.params.bend_set.note: Conifer sag (M6, bend@1): the share of each year's sag its wood keeps, with `straighten` the share of that bend it straightens each year. Set by eye from renders at 60 to 80 years: with the program's creep (0.5 and 0.02) the Pacific yew's thin, slow limbs hang down, so it keeps the milder creep the broadleaf program uses (0.1 and 0.3).

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): the sexual system its taxa state most often decides; a species whose taxa state dioecy no more often than another system bears both sexes on every plant until it states its own.

generator.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). Plants of a usual age stand below it, as the curve says. Where a flora's greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

generator.params.needle_years.note: Spec rework E6d: the pinidae program's foliage life, cones and needle bundles and ranks from each taxon's stated characters. Conifer sag (M6): green wood's density and stiffness from the Wood Handbook values the species state.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The conifers' own program (growth plan G2.3a), renamed from `conifer` and homed here: a leader laying down whorls of branches each year, with sprays of foliage and cones.

generator.spreads.params.height_max.note: What the conifer and succulent programs' height_max means: the height their Chapman-Richards curve rises toward with age and never reaches, so the tallest the plant grows, the height a flora gives as its greatest ("trees to 40 m"). Plants of a usual age stand below it, as the curve says. Where a flora's greatest is a rare record, the plant grows a little tall; a check of the grown plant against its usual height (spec rework M8) will show it.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
